draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Diveagar! The beach here faces the Arabian Sea and runs for about four kilometres, still undeveloped, with a fishing settlement at the north end and a sanctuary for migratory seabirds at the south end.
draft.hungryLine: Head to Bharadkhol, the little fishing village nearby, where vendors sell fresh fish.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Shri Siddhivinayak And Suvarna Ganesh Mandir is just 3 minutes away, and the Shri Kedarnath Mandir is about 4 minutes on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk down to the south end of the beach, where the migratory seabirds gather.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Diveagar's Suvarna Ganesh Mandir was famous for its Ganesh idol made of gold, until it was stolen on 24 March 2012.

tips.title: Rest under the suru trees.
tips.body: The beach is lined with suru (Casuarina) trees, so find some shade between walks.

tips.title: Come via Kolad.
tips.body: From the Mumbai-Goa highway, the beach is reached by turning off via Kolad or Karnala.

story.title: Six villages on the coast
story.body: The coast here strings together six villages from north to south: Velas, Musalmandi, Agar Panchaitan, Diveagar, Borli Panchatan and Karle.

story.title: Coconuts and fish
story.body: Locals fish, grow paddy and farm coconut and betel nut trees, and the fishing settlement of Velas Agar sits at the north end of the beach.

story.title: The golden Ganesh is stolen
story.body: The gold Ganesh idol of the Suvarna Ganesh Mandir drew visitors from far away, until miscreants stole it on 24 March 2012.

story.title: A quiet beach getaway
story.body: Restaurants, cottage rentals and small hotels now sit alongside the farms, and the beach is still undeveloped.
